quarantined_leads.lead: New Jersey Attorney General reporting and News 12 coverage stated that Prospect Park Councilman Anand U. Shah pleaded guilty on August 28, 2026, in Morris County Superior Court to first-degree racketeering, first-degree money laundering, and second-degree official misconduct connected to an illegal gambling operation tied to the Lucchese crime family. The plea agreement calls for a recommended 10-year state-prison sentence, forfeiture of his public office, and a permanent bar on holding public office; sentencing is scheduled for December 4, 2026.
quarantined_leads.source_title: AG Davenport Announces Prospect Park Councilman Admits Role in Illegal Gambling Operation
quarantined_leads.publisher: New Jersey Office of the Attorney General
quarantined_leads.subject_response: Shah entered a guilty plea; no separate direct statement from him was located in the current-window coverage. Earlier reporting documented that he had pleaded not guilty to the prior indictment and maintained his innocence before the current plea.
quarantined_leads.reason: The current plea and official-misconduct disposition are documented by an official state release and independently reported by News 12, but Passaic County's official candidate list identifies Shah as a Democratic candidate and other election records identify him as a Democrat. The record therefore fails A05's explicit right-wing, Republican, conservative, Trump-affiliated, or qualifying-organizational affiliation gate. It is retained as a quarantined lead rather than published; the plea is not treated as a final sentence until sentencing occurs.
